segments.content: Hey. Sorry I'm late, the previous meeting ran over.
You haven't missed anything, we were just talking about lunch.
Important topic. What's the verdict?
Noodles. It's always noodles.
Is anyone blocked on the FAQ for customers?
Not blocked, just slow. It's in decent shape.
Can we make sure that's written down somewhere? Otherwise we'll have this exact conversation again in a few weeks.
Can I get an update on the discount approval process? I lost track.
Sure. It's slower than I hoped. The hard part is behind us, I think.
Who's looking at the billing test accounts at the moment?
Me, mostly. It's basically finished, apart from tidying up.
Our invoices are confusing on their own, never mind the new plans. That might be worth fixing too.
Okay, this is the new pricing page. I took Lucas's copy and the advisory board feedback, which was mostly that people couldn't tell what's in each tier.
It's so much cleaner. The comparison table finally fits on one screen.
I like that each tier has one sentence saying who it's for. That's what the advisory board was missing.
Thanks. I've used the prices we agreed at the tiers session as placeholders, but I hear there's a discussion about Pro.
There is, and I want to settle it today. Sofia, can you share what you found?
Sure. I updated the model with real usage. Pro customers use alerts and the advanced connectors much more than we assumed. The value they get is a lot higher than the old plans suggested.
The pricing page wireframes are rough, but the structure is there.
Can we double check that with the people who actually use it every day?
Sounds sensible. I can help review it if you want a second pair of eyes.
Who's looking at the plan comparison table at the moment?
Me, mostly. It's slower than I hoped.
Can someone remind me who's taking the notes today? I want to make sure that last point is in them.
Customers mostly don't complain about the price. They complain when they don't understand what they're paying for.
I'll share my screen. Please be honest, these are early, so rough feedback is exactly what I need.
On top of that, our costs for the advanced connectors went up this quarter. At the current Pro price, the margin on heavy users is thin.
But we also told the advisory board the price, and they didn't complain. I'm worried about changing it right after showing it to them.
I understand. But they reacted to the tiers, not to the economics. I'd rather adjust now, before anything is public, than later.
From marketing, a higher price is fine if the page explains the value. And the page is much better now.
Okay. Decision. We raise the Pro tier to $59 per user per month. Starter and Enterprise stay as they are.
I'll update the model and the forecast with that number.
And I'll update the page. It's one number, so that's easy.
Right.
I'll tell Fatima, so she can mention it to the advisory board before they hear it anywhere else. I'd like their reaction.
Let's focus on the flow first and argue about colours later.
We should test the upgrade path end to end, not just the new sign-up flow.
I spent Tuesday afternoon on the invoice template. It's in decent shape, a couple of edge cases still bother me.
Where are we with the upgrade flow?
It's mostly done. It took longer than it should have.
Can I get an update on the plan names in the admin panel? I lost track.
Sure. It's slower than I hoped. I'll share it in the channel.
One worry I have is grandfathering. We need a clear rule for existing customers.
Small thing from me. I picked up the revenue model again after lunch yesterday. It's about halfway there.
On my side, work on the invoice template is slower than I hoped. It took longer than it should have.
Back to the design. Monthly versus annual billing. Do we show both on the page?
Annual billing helps cash flow a lot. If we can nudge people towards it, finance would be very happy.
Right, right.
Let's leave annual pricing open for now. I don't want to decide two pricing changes in one meeting.
Just a reminder that the team lunch is on Thursday. Please add yourself to the sheet.
Is there a vegetarian option this time?
There is. I made sure.
Then I'm in.
On my side, work on the sales talking points is about halfway there. A couple of edge cases still bother me.
I had a quick call about the plan migration script the end of last week. We're aligned, I'm reasonably happy with it.
The usage data is interesting. A small group of accounts uses most of the heavy features.
Meera, you mentioned the pricing page wireframes earlier in the week. Any news?
Some. It's further along than I expected, no surprises so far.
Great, thank you.
Small thing from me. I picked up the upgrade flow again Tuesday afternoon. It's nearly ready for review.
Small thing on the page. The Enterprise column says contact us, but it doesn't say who it's for. Can we add the seat minimum we agreed?
Yes. It helps people self-select. I'll add a line under the heading.
That should cut the small-team Enterprise requests that keep landing on sales.
Good. And let's make sure the page loads fast. Pricing pages are where people leave if they're slow.
It's mostly text and one table. It'll be quick.
What about frequently asked questions? Things like what happens at the end of the trial.
A short section at the bottom. A handful of questions at most.
Keep the answers short. If an answer needs a paragraph, the pricing is too complicated.
I'll send over the finance questions customers ask most.
When can I start using this page in the campaign drafts?
Give me a week to polish it. Then it's yours.
Great. Thanks, all. Good review.
That's all from me. Thanks for making time.
Thanks, bye.
Bye, all.
